title: Vertical procurement: latency → quality mapping and supplier trigger matrix
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create an operational deliverable that maps model latency profiles to measured output quality for three target verticals (finserv RAG, healthcare summarization, customer-support embeddings). The output will be a matrix used by Sales/Procurement and Platform to trigger procurement actions (e.g., reserve Dedicated capacity, enable quantization fallback, or flip to alternate supplier) when observed telemetry crosses thresholds. This ticket scopes the research, selects sample workloads, defines measurement methodology, runs the experiments on hosted and dedicated instances, and synthesizes a supplier trigger matrix with recommended SLO thresholds and estimated unit-cost delta.
objectives: Define vertical-specific synthetic and sampled production workloads for latency and quality testing
Measure latency distributions (p50/p95/p99) and quality (task-specific metrics) across model variants and deployment modes
Produce a ranked supplier trigger matrix: when to fallback, when to buy Dedicated capacity, and when to initiate procurement
Provide actionable thresholds and estimated monthly cost delta for each trigger so Sales and Ops can automate alerts
deliverables: CSV dataset with run-level telemetry and quality labels
Slide deck (Confluence) summarizing findings and recommended thresholds
JSON trigger matrix artifact for integration into Signal Hub
Runbook for Sales/Platform describing decision flows and follow-up experiments
methodology: Baseline selection: pick 4 representative models (open small/medium/large + provider X) per vertical
Workload design: combine synthetic worst-case prompts, sampled customer payloads, and RAG retrieval noise profiles
Metrics: latency p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, generation cost per 1k tokens, task-specific quality metrics (ROUGE/F1/semantic-similarity), customer-graded quality samples
Environments: run each workload on hosted API, Dedicated small pool, and Dedicated prewarmed pool to compare routing and fallback behavior
Analysis: compute tradeoff frontiers and identify knee points where quality gains are marginal vs latency/cost increases
acceptance_criteria: Data for all three verticals collected and validated (no missing runs)
Trigger matrix includes clear thresholds for at least 3 automated actions and estimated cost impact per month
Stakeholder sign-off from Sales Ops, Platform Reliability, and Legal on recommended procurement paths
Artifact pushed to Confluence and a pipeline point-of-contact assigned for automation integration
risks_and_tradeoffs: Using synthetic workloads may overfit thresholds — mitigated by sampling real customer payloads
Dedicated procurement actions have contractual lead times; recommend soft-thresholds before hard procurement
Quality labeling is expensive; prioritize automatic semantic metrics then escalate to human review on ambiguous cases
